title: Options and their arm documents for the Arazzo catalogue
description: Lives at `catalogue/capabilities.yaml`. Each option is behaviour the specification text leaves to the implementation, citing the sentence that leaves it; an option with a `profile` exists under that run profile alone. Its arms are keyed by the token a statement's `options` list selects one with, and each names the documents, by document id, that test it. The documents of every arm the statement does not select are skipped with `option-not-selected`, and a surface element counts as covered when every arm of its option covers it, or when the option's `decides` lists it, one arm asserts it, and every arm calls its operation. `validate` refuses an arm naming a document the catalogue does not hold, a document under two arms of one option, and a `decides` status no arm asserts or whose operation an arm does not call. `documents` states what a document needs before it runs, `floors` the workflow count each capability folder keeps, and `extension-only` the capability folders verified only over Veredictum's own extension routes.

documents.description: What a document needs from the statement before it runs, keyed by document id. `validate` refuses a key that names no document of the catalogue.

applies.description: The specification versions the document applies to, keyed by the component a statement's `spec_versions` declares a version of. Every workflow of the document is skipped version-out-of-range when the statement declares a version of a component outside its range; a component the statement does not declare decides nothing.

min.description: The first release the document applies to, inclusive.

max.description: The last release the document applies to, inclusive.

x-veredictum-cite.description: The released sentence that bounds the range, in the `arazzo-extensions` cite shape.

formats.description: The wire formats the server must serve or process for the document to run, in the statement's `tech_profiles` vocabulary. Every workflow of the document is skipped format-not-claimed when the statement's its-rest profile does not list one of them. A document that tests the refusal of a format needs nothing: it runs for a party that does not serve the format.

floors.description: The workflow count each capability folder keeps, keyed by folder name. `validate` refuses a folder without a floor, a floor naming no folder, and a folder holding fewer workflows than its floor; a test re-derives every floor from the catalogue, so a floor moves with the folder it counts.

extension-only.description: The capability folders verified only over the routes of Veredictum's own sources, the OpenAPI documents whose `info` carries `x-veredictum-non-openehr: true` and which no openEHR OAS describes. `validate` refuses a listed folder with a step calling an unmarked source, and an unlisted folder whose every step calls a marked one.

x-veredictum-cite.description: The citation, in the `arazzo-extensions` cite shape.

level.description: The requirement level of the quote: `must` (the default) for MUST, SHALL, REQUIRED or a definition, `should` for SHOULD or RECOMMENDED, `may` for MAY or OPTIONAL. A quote with no upper-case keyword is read by the same words in any other case, with "can" as a permission. `validate` refuses a level its quote's upper-case keywords disagree with, a stated `should` or `may` its quote does not say, and a citation that leaves the default `must` while its quote says "should", "can" or "may" and no requiring word; a stated `must` records that such a sentence requires in other words. A row whose failing criteria all cite `should` is failed and a warning, and never counts against a capability; a `may` criterion counts like a `must` one (RFC 2119 §5).

profile.description: The one specification profile the option exists under. A run under any other profile reads the catalogue without the option: its documents are BASE there, placed by their `x-veredictum-section`, which such a document therefore keeps, and a statement's answer to it selects nothing and is no error. Under its own profile it is an option like any other. Absent, the option exists under every profile. No openEHR spec governs this, our own design.

decides.description: The response branches the arms are the mutually exclusive answers to: for each operation, the statuses a service answers with one arm or another, and the released sentence that makes them alternatives. A listed status counts as covered when one arm asserts it and every arm calls the operation; every other element needs every arm. No openEHR spec governs this, our own design.

x-veredictum-cite.description: The citation, in the `arazzo-extensions` cite shape.
